key_insight: APO is a fully unsupervised policy-optimization framework for 3D atomic structure prediction that replaces ground-truth coordinate supervision with intrinsic, physics-based rewards.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path for modeling crystals and proteins in low-label regimes, where experimental structures are expensive or unavailable.
method: Adapts group-relative policy optimization to 3D atomic environments.
Uses a dual-reward design: a latent structural mode reward from eigen-decomposition of sample similarities and a thermodynamic stability reward.
Lets the model self-correct by favoring physically plausible configurations within each sampled group.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmarks on crystal and antibody structure prediction, where APO outperforms fully supervised baselines and improves match rates, structural fidelity, and inference efficiency.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the unsupervised reward signals and the stability of the group-sampling/eigendecomposition procedure in diverse atomic systems.
paper_title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
